findings.claim: cmd/hooks/acdsl-policy-guard.sh is an entirely new PreToolUse hook (54 new lines: path resolution, policy-mode lookup, case-pattern deny logic for the self-management surface and for strict-mode rule files) with no automated test anywhere in the diff, while its two sibling hooks added in the same commit (read-gate.sh, skill-invoke-gate.sh) each received a full cmd/tests/test_*.sh suite (test_read_gate.sh: 17 cases; test_skill_invoke_gate.sh: 9 cases).
findings.failure_scenario: A future edit to the hook's case patterns (e.g. the `rel` path-stripping, the root-walk loop, or the strict/gated mode branch) silently breaks the deny path — e.g. a quoting regression that makes `case "$rel" in acdsl/policy.json|...)` stop matching — and nothing in the shell suite or `make test` would catch it; the only check named anywhere (spec-6's Verification §) is a manual one-off `echo ... | bash cmd/hooks/acdsl-policy-guard.sh` command, never automated.
findings.fix: Add cmd/tests/test_acdsl_policy_guard.sh mirroring test_skill_invoke_gate.sh's harness: pipe synthetic PreToolUse JSON at free/gated/strict policy.json fixtures and assert deny-with-reason for the self-management surface (both modes), deny for *.acdsl/acdsl/* only in strict mode, and silent allow otherwise.
findings.evidence: Re-read cmd/hooks/acdsl-policy-guard.sh in full (54 lines, git show confirms it is wholly new vs base commit b4981b8) and grepped the full diff's test file list (cmd/tests/test_*.sh) plus all 14 spec docs for any reference to a dedicated shell test for this hook — none exists; spec-6-raw.md's own Tests section (line 31) scopes automated coverage to internal/acdsl/policy_test.go + dist_test.go + fixtures and its Verification checklist (line 543) names only a manual echo-pipe command. The claim survives: this is a genuine coverage asymmetry against the pattern set by the two sibling hooks in the same commit, not a spec violation (the spec never asked for a shell test here).

findings.claim: spec-11-change-repos-routines-ui.md's Tests table (line 508) names the required case for this file as 'squash case: two commits on an agent branch, squash-merged into main → UNPICKED 0, VERDICTS contains `squashed:2`, IN `main*`' but test_squash_transfer_reads_contained only asserts the substring `grep -q 'squashed:'`, never the count `squashed:2` the spec states.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression in evaluate_branch's squashed_n counting (routines/_lib/verdict.sh) that reports the wrong count for a two-commit squash — e.g. counting the squash-merge commit itself, or double-counting via the layer-4 sweep — would still pass this test because `grep -q 'squashed:'` matches `squashed:0`, `squashed:1`, `squashed:3`, anything; the spec's stated expectation (`squashed:2`) is never actually checked.
findings.fix: Change the assertion to `echo "$row" | grep -q 'squashed:2'` (the test's own setup commits exactly two agent commits before the squash, so the exact count is knowable and the spec names it).
findings.evidence: Re-read test_squash_transfer_reads_contained in full (lines 469-499 of the committed file via git show) and re-read spec-11-change-repos-routines-ui.md's Tests table row for this file (line 508) side by side: the setup block commits 'agent step one' then 'agent step two' (two commits) before `git merge --squash`, so `squashed:2` is the correct, knowable expected value, and the test's assertion is strictly weaker than what the spec names — the claim holds.
